core_numeric_results.interpretation: The untwisted D(A4) full 2744-sector Yasui a=1 computation agrees numerically with the standard CP2#2CPbar split presentation. This is a baseline consistency win, not an exotic separation.

case.category_twist: H3 cocycle c3-inflated omega_power=1 on A4/V4 ~= C3

core_numeric_results.interpretation: The D(A4) c3w1 category with a generator character twist on Yasui component A also evaluates to the same normalized value 12, within numeric tolerance. This validates the component-twist singleton pipeline for this case but does not produce a separating invariant.

Every ordinary separated Z/3^3 character assignment in D(A4)c3w1 stayed at the baseline value 1728. This matches the later pointed-only reduction: the relevant D(A4) directions are pure-charge bosons.

separated_character_twist_reduction.main_formula: For ordinary separated CP2#2CPbar with framings (+1,-1,-1), a universal-character assignment represented by invertibles g_h, g_e1, g_e2 has ratio theta(g_h)^-1 theta(g_e1) theta(g_e2) relative to the untwisted split value.
proof_draft_content: For a modular category, a universal grading character is represented by an invertible simple object g via monodromy.
The +1 Gauss sum obeys tau_+(g)=theta_g^-1 tau_+(1) by reindexing X -> g tensor X.
The -1 Gauss sum obeys tau_-(g)=theta_g tau_-(1) in the unitary/ribbon setting.
The split unlink factorizes over components, so only the pointed/invertible quadratic form remains.
separated_character_twist_reduction.consequence: On the ordinary separated presentation, F-symbols, R-symbols, fusion multiplicities, and non-pointed simple objects disappear except through the baseline Gauss sums. Therefore this cheap test filters pointed/simple-current phases, not genuinely non-pointed exotic information.
not_yet_proved: A fully cited theorem-level writeup for arbitrary non-separated surgery links.
A formal convention comparison for every premodular/nonmodular Yetter twist setting.

candidate_filtering_results.criterion: For untwisted D(G), invertible simples are (z,chi) with z in Z(G) and chi in Hom(G,C*), and theta_(z,chi)=chi(z). The ordinary split character test can be nonbaseline exactly when some central element survives in G_ab, equivalently the natural map Z(G)->G_ab is nonzero.
candidate_filtering_results.important_correction: Z(A4) is trivial, while A4_ab is Z/3. The Z/3 directions used by D(A4) are pure charges, hence bosonic with twist 1.

summary.group: Dic_3, the order-12 dicyclic / binary-dihedral group Q12

candidate_filtering_results.interpretation: This refutes the naive guess that every D(G) is split-test useless. However the signal is still only a pointed metric-group phase, not a non-pointed F/R effect.

SU(3)_2 gives a clean simple-current phase on the ordinary separated presentation. It is a useful future candidate only after building/importing actual SU(3)_2 F/R data for the non-separated Yasui link.

The split presentation sees only the SU(2)_k simple current phase. Prior saved Yasui a=1 SU(2) checks, including the committed k=8 all-alpha comparison, do not show a Yasui-vs-standard difference. Treat SU(2)_k as poor evidence for this route unless a sharper non-separated mechanism is identified.
